title: Substrate component (version registry)
description: FLAGGED EXTENSION beyond PLAN §2's five objects — see README 'Deviations'. The registry entry for one shared substrate function (propagator, surrogate, scorer, cross, decimate, ...). PLAN §3 (Q6) requires every shared function to 'carry a version/hash and live behind a versioned, gated interface'; this is that registry. It is what makes the `depends_on: component@version` edge on claim cards and the `substrate_versions` stamp on run records RESOLVE to something — and therefore what makes automatic blast-radius computable ('the thing that cost s001–s066 becomes one line'). One file per component; `versions` is the append-only history.

id.description: Short stable id used as the LHS of `component@version` refs (e.g. 'propagator', 'surrogate', 'scorer'). NOTE: this bare id is what run_record.substrate_versions keys and claim_card.depends_on reference — keep it terse and never reuse it.

path.description: Repo-relative source path of the canonical implementation.

tier.description: Only substrate-tier code is versioned here. Scratch (experiments/sXXX.py) is deliberately NOT registered (two-tier model, Q7).

interface.description: One-line description of the versioned public interface (the gated seam).

functions.description: Optional, hand-authored breakdown of the load-bearing functions this component is made of — the comprehension granularity beneath the single versioned interface. Display-only and HAND-MAINTAINED: the version/hash/blast-radius live at the COMPONENT, never per-function (per-function blast would drown the 's001-s066 = one line' signal). For the AST-grounded, drift-checked view of these functions in the wider pipeline, curate them as overlay units in the machinery map (render/machinery_overlay.json) — the derive cross-checks THOSE against the code, not this array.

name.description: Function name as it appears in `path`.

signature.description: The def line (args), trimmed — e.g. 'propagate_euler(q0, omega, times)'.

role.description: Plain-language one-liner: what this function does in the pipeline (inputs→outputs).

line.description: 1-based line of the def in `path` (best-effort, hand-maintained — NOT auto-refreshed; the machinery map carries the AST-authoritative line for the same function when it is curated as an overlay unit).

current_version.description: The version currently in force. Must equal versions[-1].version. A run stamped with any other version, or a claim depending on any other version, is in the blast radius of the latest bump.

promoted_from.description: run_record id this Tool was operationalised from (Tool -> promoted-from -> Experiment, ADR-0005). Null for tools that predate the run-record store or were authored directly. Records the moment a scratch experiment became reusable substrate.

canon.description: ADR-0007. Whether this is the CANONICAL Tool of its variant family — the one you get by default when you name the Tool. False = a meaningful variant (see variant_of). Accidental copies are NOT variants; they collapse into the canon Tool's default_params.

variant_of.description: ADR-0007. id of the canonical Tool this is a MEANINGFUL variant of (the variant-of edge; mirrors Pipeline rivalry). Null for canon Tools. Validated to resolve to an existing substrate_component.

entry_point.description: ADR-0007. The single canonical callable seam for the run-button: 'repo/relative/path.py:function'. The executor (#15) invokes THIS to 'run the Tool on an input'. Binds to canonical code (Q1 reflect-not-own); the drift-check refuses to run if it no longer resolves or its hash moved.

ports.description: ADR-0007. Typed input/output signature written in ARTIFACT TYPES — each entry's VALUE is a glossary_term id (the glossary doubles as the port type-system). Two forms (transition): the legacy FLAT LIST ['ia-cloud'] (describes types, not bound to return-keys — NOT reifiable), and the KEYED MAP {'<return-key/kwarg/tuple-position-name>': '<glossary_term id>'} which binds each name to its type. The keyed map is what `loop/artifacts.py` needs to reify outputs ('recognised materials only') and to type-check re-fed inputs. e.g. {input:{'q0_arr':'ia-cloud'}, output:{'q_pool_wxyz':'ia-cloud'}}. All values validated to resolve to existing glossary terms.

input.description: Input artifact types. Keyed map {kwarg_name: glossary_term id} (preferred — enables re-feed type-check), or legacy flat list [glossary_term id, ...].

output.description: Output artifact types. Keyed map {return-key/tuple-position-name: glossary_term id} (preferred — required to reify the output as an artifact_instance), or legacy flat list [glossary_term id, ...] (described but NOT reified).

default_params.description: ADR-0007. Default parameterisation. The lever that collapses accidental copies into ONE parameterised Tool: variation that is just a different param value lives HERE, not in a new Tool. e.g. {tol_mag:0.10, n_samples:1000000, surrogate:'v2', pool:24}.

current_hash.description: Content hash (e.g. git blob sha or sha256 of the source) of the current implementation. If the file changes but current_version does not, that is a silent change the gate flags (an undocumented bump).

versions.description: Append-only version history, oldest first. Appending an entry (a bump) is the blast-radius trigger.

change_reason.description: Why it changed (e.g. 'ω-sign convention fix +0.5→-0.5; invalidated s001-s066').

is_bug_fix.description: True if the bump corrects a bug (vs a feature/refactor). Bug-fix bumps are the dangerous ones — they retroactively invalidate dependent evidence.
